cyclic nucleotide analogues attenuate thrombin-induced alterations in the activity and pH set point of the Na/H exchanger in human platelets, and that this effect is mediated through a mechanism which involves inhibition of thrombin-induced increase in cytosolic Ca.

the role of cyclic AMP and cyclic GMP in modulating the Na/H anti-port in thrombin-activated human platelets.
the role of cyclic AMP and cyclic GMP as second messengers in the regulation of the Na/H exchanger in human platelets, and their effect on thrombogenic processes.
the role of cAMP and cyclic GMP in the modulation of the Na/H exchanger in human platelets and other cell types.
